Subject: RE: Order Form draft — a few clarifying points

Marcus — thanks for the draft. Our procurement and tax teams reviewed and flagged three items we need to align on before legal proceeds: 

1) Pricing breakpoint: BluePeak's finance needs an explicit definition of the "pricing breakpoint" in the schedule — how usage tiers are evaluated (calendar month vs invoice month) and whether we bill overage at the higher or lower tier if monthly usage crosses a band.

2) Minimum commit cadence: The order form references an annual minimum commit with quarterly invoicing. Can you confirm whether minimums can be satisfied across entity invoices (we may split POs across subsidiaries)? If not, our procurement will request entity-level language.

3) Taxes & withholding: Our tax group needs clarity on who bears withholding taxes for US-sourced services and whether Redwood will gross-up if reverse-charge/VAT doesn't apply. We attached a redline (BluePeak_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) with markup and a copy of our tax certificate.

Can you loop in finance/legal at Redwood and share proposed language? Also helpful if you can attach the pricing schedule in native form (xlsx).

Thanks — Sally

Subject: RE: Order Form draft — a few clarifying points

Sally — really appreciate the clear redline and the tax cert. Quick responses below and then I pasted our updated clause drafts for legal: 

High-level answers:
- Pricing breakpoint: we evaluate tiers on invoice-period usage (i.e., calendar month aligned to the invoice). If a single invoice month crosses bands, overage is billed pro rata at the tiered unit price for the threshold crossed — but for clarity we'll add an explicit definition and an illustrative example in the schedule.
- Minimum commit cadence: Redwood is fine with cross-entity satisfaction of annual minimums if BluePeak provides a single PO umbrella and a primary billing entity is designated on the order form. If BluePeak needs strict per-entity minimums, we will need to adjust invoicing/contracting to reflect separate order forms per entity.
- Taxes & withholding: standard position is customer is responsible for all taxes, duties, and withholdings. Redwood will consider gross-up where contractually required and where Redwood has presence/registration in the taxing jurisdiction. 

I attached a native pricing schedule (RWI_pricing_schedule_BP4821.xlsx) and a redline of the order form with proposed language. Below are the suggested snippets for the order form: 

-- Pricing breakpoint (new definition to add to Exhibit A) --
"Pricing Breakpoint" means the monthly unit-usage thresholds set out in the Pricing Schedule. Usage tiers are evaluated per invoice period (calendar month). If usage in an invoice period spans multiple tiers, charges for the period will be calculated pro rata across applicable tiers. Example: if Tier A covers 0–100k tokens and Tier B covers 100k–500k tokens, and month usage = 130k tokens, the first 100k are charged at Tier A price, the remaining 30k at Tier B price.

-- Minimum Commit (Order Form section 3) --
Customer may satisfy the Annual Minimum Commit via aggregated invoices across affiliates provided that (i) Customer identifies a primary billing entity on the Order Form; and (ii) Customer furnishes a single umbrella PO referencing this Order Form. If Customer requires per-entity minimum enforcement, separate Order Forms are required.

-- Taxes & Withholding (Order Form section 7) --
All fees are exclusive of taxes, duties or other governmental assessments. Customer is responsible for taxes imposed on Customer’s purchase (including withholding taxes), except for taxes based on Redwood’s net income. If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes, Customer must provide evidence of such withholding and any available relief; Redwood will reasonably cooperate with Customer to claim treaty benefits or refunds. Where applicable law requires gross-up of payments, the parties will negotiate in good faith an appropriate gross-up.

Next steps: kimberly_park (cc'd) from Legal and ben_carter from Commercial will take the redline and provide one consolidated clean-redline we can send back to BluePeak Legal. Laura will confirm whether Operations can accept umbrella PO flows. Expect internal reply by EOD.

Thanks — Marcus

Quick internal note before we send back to BluePeak Legal. High priority items we need to settle: 

1) Gross-up policy: legal will not commit to automatic gross-ups. We should offer gross-up only where there's a legal obligation (evidence from customer + jurisdictional rule). That matches what Marcus suggested.
2) Umbrella PO risk: ops (Laura) flagged that accepting umbrella POs across entities increases invoicing reconciliation work. Laura — please confirm whether finance can accept umbrella PO with primary billing entity and we document reconciliation cadence (quarterly).
3) Pricing examples: ask pricing ops to include two worked examples in the pricing schedule (month with single-band usage vs month crossing bands). Ben, can you take the pricing examples and update the attached xlsx?

I propose we produce a single consolidated redline that: (a) adds the explicit Pricing Breakpoint definition, (b) includes the minimum commit language allowing umbrella POs with primary billing entity, and (c) preserves customer tax-responsibility language but includes a clause requiring evidence for withholding and a good-faith gross-up negotiation path.
